chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The keeper of the deposit and the merchant are two trusted parties. And he said: If the item borrowed for use perishes in the possession of the borrower, he is not liable for it unless a condition was stipulated upon him.
ai.seo_question: Is a borrower liable if the borrowed item is lost accidentally?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the fiduciary standards in commercial transactions, affirming that trustees and merchants are presumed trustworthy (mu'taman) unless proven otherwise. It further clarifies the principle of *daman* (liability) for borrowed items (*ariyyah*), establishing that accidental loss does not incur compensation unless a specific condition of guarantee was explicitly agreed upon, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on contractual freedom and risk allocation.
